subject: Food Science
title: Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria.

hook.text: 80% of US antibiotics go to farm animals, not humans. The result: superbugs emerging in our food supply.

buildup.text: Antibiotics in animal feed promote growth and prevent disease in crowded conditions. Bacteria adapt and resist.

discovery.text: MRSA and antibiotic-resistant Salmonella have been found on retail chicken and pork. Cooking kills them—but handling spreads them.

twist.text: The EU banned growth-promoting antibiotics in livestock in 2006. The US followed partially in 2017. Many countries haven't.

climax.text: WHO warns that antibiotic resistance could kill 10 million people annually by 2050 if trends continue.

punchline.text: We made superbugs on the farm. Now they're on our plates.

quiz.question: What percentage of US antibiotics are used in farm animals?
